import html # Template for rendering a blog post. # It contains placeholders `{title}` and `{body}` which will be safely escaped BLOG_FORMAT = """

{title}

{body}
""" def render_blog_post(title: str, body: str) -> str: """ Render a blog post for safe display on a web page. Parameters ---------- title : str The title of the blog post. body : str The main content of the blog post. Returns ------- str A string containing the sanitized HTML representation of the blog post. Notes ----- * The function uses `html.escape` to neutralize any HTML or JavaScript that could be injected by the user, protecting against XSS attacks. * The resulting string is well‑formed and can be safely inserted into an HTML document. This mitigates CWE-707 by ensuring the output is properly escaped before being rendered. Raises ------ ValueError If either `title` or `body` is not a string. """ if not isinstance(title, str) or not isinstance(body, str): raise ValueError("Both title and body must be strings") # Escape user input to prevent injection safe_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(body, quote=True) # Format the final HTML snippet return BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_title, body=safe_body)
